Senses.Explanation: To become obstructed along every route or at every turn. The phrase diagnoses fixation, conceptual impurity, mishandled teaching formulas, or ongoing course that converts whatever it meets into an impediment. Huanglong says an object lodged in the chest remains before the eyes and produces obstruction at every turn. Dahui says mixed poison entering the mind makes one obstructed wherever one turns. Linquan warns that inadequate grounding in Caodong teaching repeatedly meets obstruction. Yunju contrasts realization’s unimpeded function with loss, which produces obstruction everywhere.
